review_comments_data.body:
Hello @lebaphi - this test shouldn't fail, should it?

The hidden wargame shouldn't be listed, so it can't be present as `currentWargame`, can it.

I _guess_ this is handling some edge case.  Based on it being an edge case, I suggest the notification at line 21 below be changed to:
`Error: hidden wargame should not be available. Not opening.`

Hi @IanMayo, the hidden wargame shouldn't be listed, right. This handles the case:
- in the client-side, the user loads the list of 3 games
- at this time on the server-side, the admin hide 1 of 3 games
- in the client-side, the user does not reload the page and chooses the hidden game then press enter.

=> we should handle this case and show an error message. I will update the error message.

issues.title: As a Game Control, I wish to be able to hide games
issues.body:
A game control may be working with a number of wargames, and may choose to hide some snapshots (or old games) from the players - to ensure the players go into the correct wargame.

The list of games in the admin page could have a checkbox to indicate which ones are presented to players.

I _guess_ we would store this in the `pouchdb_all_dbs` collection.  The alternative is to have a `visible` element in the wargame, but we'd have to load/parse all the wargames in order to show the welcome page.

This requires a degree of familiarity with PouchDb.

Sadly it looks like it isn't possible via `_all_dbs`.  I suspect we could only achieve this via a custom table of databases.

I guess an alternate strategy is to use a leading underscore as a `hidden` marker.  So, we rename hidden games to have a leading underscore. That's not all that bad - since we won't be expecting users to load/play a hidden game.

So, in the admin UI we could provide a `visible` checkbox in the wargame listing.  Clicking this checkbox (or eye icon) would (secretly) add/remove a leading underscore for that wargame.
